title: Hourglass pricing conservation scratchpad
content:
Goal: quick, dirty proto for a ‘conservation’ credit model — encourage small steady usage, penalize wasteful bursts that force higher infra footprint. Intuition: convert GPU-hour + infra into an hourglass-shaped credit that depletes faster under high concurrency/latency-sensitive patterns.

Assumptions (back of envelope):
- p3-equivalent rental cost: $2.40 / GPU-hour (blended) -> conservative $3.00/hr including infra/overheads
- avg tokens per second at 8k context: 30 tokens/sec per request in long-chat scenario
- effective tokens per GPU-hour = 30 tok/s * 3600s * active_concurrency_factor. but batching complicates.
- baseline effective throughput (continuous streaming): 108k tokens / GPU-hr at single stream. but with batching we can do much more. set conservative unified tokens/GPU-hr = 25M tokens (for mixed workloads)

Token unit cost baseline: $3.00 / 25,000,000 = $0.00000012 per token -> $0.12 per 1M tokens (internal cost). Target gross margin 70% -> price ~ $0.40 / 1M tokens. Current hosted floor = $0.35/1M for emb-like? (note: check comps)

Hourglass credit idea: each user session gets an "hourglass" of N credits tied to expected steady-state usage. Credits deplete at base rate for tokens consumed, BUT depletion accelerates when requests are bursty (high concurr or short TTL on KV cache) or low batching efficiency. That acceleration is implemented by a multiplier M = f(concurrency, latency_tier, cache_hit_rate).

Example mechanics (toy):
- Assign 1000 credits per seat for a month (maps loosely -> 2.5M tokens at base rate).
- base token-to-credit: 2500 tokens = 1 credit (so 1000 credits -> 2.5M tokens)
- multiplier: M = 1 + max(0, concurrency-1)*0.4 + (1-cache_hit_rate)*0.6 + latency_tier_bonus
  - concurrency measured per-minute averaged over session
  - latency_tier_bonus (if routing to L4 latency path) = 0.5

So a 3-concurrency session with cache_hit_rate 0.2 routed to low-latency path: M = 1 + (3-1)*0.4 + 0.8*0.6 + 0.5 = 1 + 0.8 + 0.48 + 0.5 = 2.78 -> effective credits consumed per token nearly x2.8 (discourages unbatched concurrency).

Why this might work: aligns incentives — customers optimize batching, cache reuse, and conversational sessionization. Also gives a natural knob for enterprise to buy latency premium credits (e.g., purchase low-latency multipliers removed for a surcharge).

Edge cases / open q's:
- How to measure cache_hit_rate consistently across hosted/dedicated/private? Need unified telemetry.
- Free-tier exploitation vector: bots spinning idle sessions with 1 tok every 30s to hold KV cache. Need TTL-based decay on hourglass (credits evaporate slowly over idle periods).
- Refunds / charge disputes: define explicit mapping tokens->credits + explain multipliers in billing UI. UX clarity required.

Pricing sketch for tiers using hourglass lens:
- Starter: 1k credits/mo, basic latency (M floor 1.0), $9/mo -> implied $9 / 2.5M tokens -> $3.6 per 1M tokens public price (but credit price vs token price decoupled)
- Growth: 10k credits/mo, $70/mo, includes 10% of credits at reduced multiplier for burst + 1 free dedicated routing slot (soft).
- Scale: custom commits, purchase bulk credits with locked M floor and SLA. Add-on: low-latency pool credits at 1.6x price.

Quick sensitivity (back-of-envelope):
- If base internal cost changes to $6/GPU-hr (cloud spike), tokens/GPU-hr unchanged -> internal token cost doubles -> need to raise price OR increase required credits per token. Hourglass model helps by shifting burst cost to multiplier rather than base price.

Implementation notes / tracker TODOs:
- [ ] prototype multiplier telemetry in staging (latency tier + concurrency + cache hits)
- [ ] add simple UI wording for multipliers, show example scenarios on billing page
- [ ] simulate 1k customers with random session profiles to estimate realized revenue and infra risk (Monte Carlo)
- [ ] gatefree-tier: implement idle-decay (credits evaporate 1%/day after 24h idle)

Random thoughts: could map hourglass to time-windowed quotas (credits refill per rolling 30d), or take the other route: credits are per-session and nonrefill (encourages renew). Also consider hybrid: credits + meter for egress / storage.

Notes-to-self: run small A/B with 500 customers replacing token-based buckets with hourglass for 30d; measure change in batching, cache hit rate, and per-customer infra cost. If we can move 20% of traffic into higher batching by design, unit economics improve significantly.

Links to prior experiments: see linked JIRA and GH above. Slack thread: #pricing-discuss (search "hourglass").

Unresolved: exact mapping of credits->1M tokens for different model families (small vs Llama3/7B vs Llama3/70B); maybe maintain model-family multipliers to keep fairness.

End of scratchpad (that's messy — revisit after Monte Carlo).
